an4.162:1.1: “Monks, there are these four modes of practice.
an4.162:2.1: “And which is painful practice with slow intuition?
an4.162:2.2: There is the case where a certain individual is normally of an intensely passionate nature. He perpetually experiences pain & distress born of passion.
an4.162:2.3: Or he is normally of an intensely aversive nature. He perpetually experiences pain & distress born of aversion.
an4.162:2.4: Or he is normally of an intensely deluded nature. He perpetually experiences pain & distress born of delusion.
an4.162:2.6: the faculty of conviction, the faculty of persistence, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of discernment—appear weakly.
an4.162:2.7: Because of their weakness, he attains only slowly the immediacy1 that leads to the ending of the effluents.
an4.162:2.8: This is called painful practice with slow intuition.
an4.162:3.1: “And which is painful practice with quick intuition?
an4.162:3.2: There is the case where a certain individual is normally of an intensely passionate nature. He perpetually experiences pain & distress born of passion.
an4.162:3.3: Or he is normally of an intensely aversive nature. He perpetually experiences pain & distress born of aversion.
an4.162:3.4: Or he is normally of an intensely deluded nature. He perpetually experiences pain & distress born of delusion.
an4.162:3.6: the faculty of conviction, the faculty of persistence, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of discernment—appear intensely.
an4.162:3.7: Because of their intensity, he attains quickly the immediacy that leads to the ending of the effluents.
an4.162:3.8: This is called painful practice with quick intuition.
an4.162:4.1: “And which is pleasant practice with slow intuition?
an4.162:4.2: There is the case where a certain individual is normally not of an intensely passionate nature. He does not perpetually experience pain & distress born of passion.
an4.162:4.3: Or he is normally not of an intensely aversive nature. He does not perpetually experience pain & distress born of aversion.
an4.162:4.4: Or he is normally not of an intensely deluded nature. He does not perpetually experience pain & distress born of delusion.
an4.162:4.6: the faculty of conviction, the faculty of persistence, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of discernment—appear weakly.
an4.162:4.7: Because of their weakness, he attains only slowly the immediacy that leads to the ending of the effluents.
an4.162:4.8: This is called pleasant practice with slow intuition.
an4.162:5.1: “And which is pleasant practice with quick intuition?
an4.162:5.2: There is the case where a certain individual is normally not of an intensely passionate nature. He does not perpetually experience pain & distress born of passion.
an4.162:5.3: Or he is normally not of an intensely aversive nature. He does not perpetually experience pain & distress born of aversion.
an4.162:5.4: Or he is normally not of an intensely deluded nature. He does not perpetually experience pain & distress born of delusion.
an4.162:5.6: the faculty of conviction, the faculty of persistence, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of discernment—appear intensely.
an4.162:5.7: Because of their intensity, he attains quickly the immediacy that leads to the ending of the effluents.
an4.162:5.8: This is called pleasant practice with quick intuition.
an4.162:5.9: “These are the four modes of practice.”
